---
title: Customs brokerage
department: logistics
status: current
---
Northwind acts as a direct representative for customs clearance in the European
Union and as an indirect representative in the United Kingdom. The distinction
matters because it determines who carries the liability when a declaration is
wrong, and the support team should never promise a customer that Northwind will
absorb a duty reassessment.

A commercial invoice must accompany every non-document shipment crossing a
customs border. The invoice must state the incoterm, the country of origin, the
gross and net weight, and a tariff classification for every line. A shipment
tendered without a tariff classification will be held and an incident raised
against the shipper's account.

Tariff classifications follow the Harmonised System. The classification team
maintains the mapping between Northwind product categories and HS codes, and
reviews it whenever the World Customs Organisation publishes an amendment.

HS 8471.30 | Portable automatic data processing machines under ten kilograms | duty rate 0.0 percent | requires model number on the invoice line
HS 8517.62 | Machines for reception and transmission of voice or data | duty rate 0.0 percent | requires radio approval reference
HS 6110.20 | Jerseys and pullovers of cotton, knitted | duty rate 12.0 percent | requires fibre composition
HS 3926.90 | Other articles of plastics | duty rate 6.5 percent | requires material description

Duty and tax are billed to the party named in the incoterm. Where the incoterm is
DDP the charges are billed to the shipper's account within two business days of
clearance. Where the incoterm is DAP the consignee is invoiced directly by the
clearing agent and Northwind has no visibility of payment.

Clearance delays are reported as an incident only when the delay exceeds the
transit commitment for the tier. A shipment held for a routine documentary check
inside the committed transit window is not an incident and the escalation team
will close it without action.
